LanguageData.DDAF_PlayerDiplomacy: Diplomacy changes can involve your faction
LanguageData.DDAF_PlayerDiplomacyDesc: About the number of times per year set below, a random NPC faction makes peace with you (if hostile) or turns hostile. Goodwill moves just far enough to change the relation (peace: 0, war: -75). Follows the diplomacy change, permanent enemy, exclude Empire and ideo bloc settings above. Added by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_BasePerYearDesc: Dynamic Diplomacy also adds this event to every storyteller, independent of the extra chance (originally 2-4 diplomacy changes and 3-5 conquests per year). 0 turns that off. Set by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_ExtraPerYearDesc: Rolled every 6 hours. Replaces the old whole-percent chance (1% per 6 hours = 2.4 times per year), so lower values are possible. An event that finds no valid target does nothing. Set by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_ConquestBattleStart: {0} forces are about to engage defensive forces in {1} settlement of {2}. The fighting will start soon.
LanguageData.DDAF_BaseSiegeChanceDesc: Chance that a conquest battle is fought on a map generated like the contested settlement: the defender holds its base with the garrison that map comes with (Custom Base Framework bases and Better Settlement Defense roles apply when installed), and the attacker uses the basic arena AI. 0 turns it off. Added by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_Pirates: Pirates drop in on a stronger defender
LanguageData.DDAF_PiratesDesc: The stronger the defenders of a battle are than the attackers (for example a well-defended base), the likelier a pirate faction hostile to both sides drops in on the defenders by drop pod. The gap 1 - attacker strength / defender strength (fighters' combat power: 1.5x the attackers is 33%, 2x is 50%, 5x is 80%) is the chance, and also the pirates' share of the conquest threat points, up to half. The pirates fight for themselves and do not decide the outcome. Needs an industrial or later permanently hostile faction. Added by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_KeepSurvivorsDesc: When a battle without your colonists ends, living fighters leave the map and become world pawns, like raiders who leave a map, instead of being deleted. They can show up again later in raids, caravans or other battles. Downed fighters of the losing side are taken prisoner by the winners instead and may join them over time (unwaveringly loyal ones never do). They also escape now and then (mean 60 days), and go free once the two factions make peace or the captors are defeated. Added by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_TechWeightedExpansionDesc: When a new settlement is founded, the nearby settlement whose faction gets it is picked with weight 1.5 tribal, 1.3 medieval, 1 industrial, 0.8 spacer, 0.6 ultra, so factions with weaker armies make up ground elsewhere. Off: every nearby settlement counts the same, as in Dynamic Diplomacy. Added by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_RazeChanceLowDesc: Razing is the only way settlements leave the world. Below {0}%, the world soon reaches the expansion limit and expansion stops, so tech-weighted expansion and ruin resettling stop with it, and few ruins are left for clearing. Warning added by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_WarnNoSimulatedConquest: "Simulate in-game battle" is off, so no battles are fought on a map and this does nothing.
LanguageData.DDAF_WarnNoExpansion: Expansion events are off, so this does nothing.
LanguageData.DDAF_WarnNoDistanceCalc: Distance-based calculation is off, so alliances never form.
LanguageData.DDAF_ExpansionLimitReachedDesc: The world already has {0} settlements, above this limit, so expansion has stopped, and tech-weighted expansion and ruin resettling with it. Raise the limit, or let razed settlements bring the count down. Warning added by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_SettlementCleanupDesc: One-off cleanup to 80% of the expansion limit ({0} settlements), so expansion can run again. Each NPC faction gives up settlements in proportion to how many it has and keeps at least {1}. Settlements off the road network go first, road ends last. Each removed settlement leaves a ruin that is kept only on roads, like ruin clearing. Settlements you are involved with (maps, your caravans, quests, trade requests) are left alone. Added by Dynamic Diplomacy Fixes & Tweaks.
LanguageData.DDAF_SettlementCleanupConfirm: Remove settlements from {0} down to {1} (target {2})? Each NPC faction keeps at least {3}. This cannot be undone.
LanguageData.DDAF_SettlementCleanupNothing: No settlement can be removed: every faction is down to {0}, or the rest are in use by you.
LanguageData.DDAF_SettlementCleanupDone: Removed {0} settlements; {1} ruins left on roads.
